mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up Ali and Wallace's journey, I hope you’re feeling the power of a story that changes how we see the world. This wasn’t just about setting the record straight—it was about tuning in to what’s often overlooked, listening for the quieter voices, and honoring all the different ways we come to understand things. Keep these reminders close as you go forward: Every discovery? It’s built on countless unseen hands and shared effort. The stories we choose to tell decide who’s remembered—and who’s left in the shadows. Real collaboration means listening, sharing, and truly valuing every kind of knowledge. You can help change the narrative—one story, one voice at a time. And justice? It always starts with recognizing others, and that starts with curiosity and care. So, here’s what this means for you: whether you’re a student, a teacher, a scientist, or just someone who cares about fairness, remember—history is always being written. You have the power to ask new questions, to seek out the stories that haven’t been told, and to make space for voices that have been missing. This work isn’t always easy or quick, but it matters deeply. Let Ali’s story remind you: every life counts. Our world becomes richer, kinder, and more honest when we refuse to let anyone be forgotten. Carry that lesson with you. Let it shape how you see, how you listen, and how you share your own stories. After all, the past isn’t just something behind us—it’s alive in every choice you make today.
